title: From gross income to taxable income — the Chen family
instructions: Lin and Wei Chen file jointly for 2025. They have two children, ages 6 and 10. Compute the amounts below (round to the nearest dollar). Assume the QBI deduction is below the threshold and that QBI is net profit reduced by the deductible half of SE tax.

exhibits.title: Income
exhibits.content:
- Combined wages: **$150,000**
- Interest on a bank account: **$2,000**
- Wei's Schedule C (graphic design) net profit: **$30,000**

exhibits.title: Payments
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount |
|---|---:|
| HSA contribution (family HDHP coverage), made by the Chens | 4,000 |
| Unreimbursed medical expenses | 15,000 |
| State income tax | 9,000 |
| Real estate tax on their home | 8,000 |
| Mortgage interest (acquisition debt $420,000) | 12,000 |
| Cash contributions to their church | 3,000 |

rows.label: Deduction for half of SE tax
Total itemized deductions
rows.explanation: 1,809 + 17,000 (SALT under the $40,000 cap) + 12,000 + 3,000 = **33,809** — more than the $31,500 standard deduction, so they itemize.

rows.label: QBI deduction
rows.explanation: 20% × (30,000 − 2,119) = **5,576** (less than 20% of taxable income before QBI).

reviewNote: Relies on 2025 amounts set by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (standard deduction, child tax credit, or SALT cap). Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.
